newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks extend gains at opening.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks extend gains at opening.

text.p: The Australian share market extended Wednesday's strong gains at the opening on Thursday.

Traders said that with offshore markets providing little inspiration, local investors were consolidating Wednesday's strong performance with ex-dividend and option-related trade driving much of the turnover. September series options expire on Thursday while several large companies go ex-dividend.
The All Ordinaries index was up 9.3 points at 2262.1 in early trading.
"It's been a positive start," said dealer Paul Ford of Shaw Stockbroking. "Wall Street didn't give us much indication so we are consolidating after yesterday's interest rate non-event."
Pointing to options expiries and the imminent September share index futures contract close-out on Monday, Ford said volumes could be driven by these events as much as any other.
"You may see some artificial buying with options expiry today and some arbitrage trade with the futures," Ford said.
Banks were sought after as investors chased dividend yields with both ANZ and National Australia reaching new highs of A$7.15 and A$13.15 respectively.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about three to one, while about 40 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
